purpose: Describe the small Google tag used on Mythical’s public shop window. The tag is not part of the game. It starts with analytics and advertising storage turned off, asks visitors before enabling analytics, sends only a simple public-page visit after an affirmative choice, turns advertising features off, and never receives a game save, creature name, account number, email, age, child detail, full query string, or user ID from Mythical. A visitor can say no. The tag is checked in the page source, the consent helper, the public privacy page, and both production hosting policies before release.

productionEvidence.limitation: The current browser already held a prior visitor choice, so this check did not delete browser data or replay the first-visit banner. No Google Analytics property, Realtime report, retention setting, or exported event row was inspected. Deployment is proven; correct property-side receipt remains unproven.

sourceChecks.purpose: tag id, consent default, and game exclusion
alternate production script and connection permissions

nextDecision: Deployment is no longer the question: the correct Google tag is present on the live public homepage, the privacy wording is live, and the game runtime does not load the tag script. Before any number is trusted, Kevin must open the Google Analytics property he controls and confirm the property belongs to Mythical Void, the retention choice is appropriate, and a fresh private-browser test produces no event before consent, no event after “No thanks”, and only the allowed canonical public-page and broad Play or Share events after “Allow analytics”. The person who can remove the tag must also be named. Until that property-side check is complete, absence of data must not be called zero interest, and any visible count must not be used as a player, child, conversion, retention, or advertising claim.
